newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar jumps to 127.45 yen in late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar jumps to 127.45 yen in late Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar jumped as high as 127.45 yen in late Thursday Tokyo dealings after stop-loss buying and short-covering were triggered, propelling the dollar to its highest level since August 1992.
Rises had been thwarted for several days by sales made in an effort to protect options positions with a knock-out point at 127.30 yen.
These options would have given holders the right to buy dollars at 123 or 124 yen, well below current levels, unless the dollar hit the knock-out price of 127.30 yen before expiry.
The majority of these options had been set to expire in New York time later on Thursday, although some dealers said a smaller amount was set to expire at 0600 GMT in Tokyo.

Stop-loss buying orders placed at 127.20 yen were triggered, sending the greenback quickly to 127.30 yen and knocking out the remaining options prior to their expiry. This in turn set off a flurry of additional stop-loss buying, taking the dollar even higher, dealers said.

But the dollar apparently ran into exporter sales near 127.50 yen, blocking further gains. Dealers said there also seemed to be additional sales connected to options with a strike price at 127.50 yen, with further stop-loss buying near 127.55-60 yen.
"If this is touched off, we could well see the dollar head towards 127.80 yen," one city bank dealer said.

Although the greenback's gains heighten concerns about the possibility of dollar-selling intervention by the Bank of Japan (BOJ), dealers said it remains difficult to predict the likelihood of such moves.

"It is still likely to be difficult to intervene successfully at this point, particularly if the BOJ ends up intervening alone, as the market remains relatively neutral in terms of positions," an agricultural bank dealer said.

"In addition, unless the intervention were massive enough to push the dollar down to around 125 yen or lower in one shot, it would only serve to slow the dollar's rise, not halt it, meaning the BOJ would then have to intervene again," he added.
The last such dollar-selling intervention carried out by the BOJ was in August 1992, when the dollar was at the upper end of the 127-128 yen range.

In a statement issued after their meeting last week, Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank heads said they agreed that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility and significant deviations from fundamentals are undesirable.

The greenback had been strong since the morning after U.S. data released on Wednesday showed the economy growing at a robust annual rate of 5.6 percent in the first quarter. The numbers sent New York stocks soaring above 7,000 for the first time since March 13 and also pushed bonds higher.
